title: NIST: Astatine (At, Z=85) has bracketed mass number [210], not an atomic-weight interval
summary: NIST prints the standard atomic weight field of Astatine (At, Z=85) as [210], with the isotope rows in the same file.
body: PubChem's periodic-table row names atomic number 85, symbol At, as Astatine. The NIST compositions file prints the standard-atomic-weight field of Astatine as [210]. Brackets around that single value are the mass number of the most stable isotope, as NIST's column note defines them. They are not an atomic-weight interval and not a measured relative atomic mass of a sample. The notes field on this element's rows is blank. Isotope rows in the same file: At-210 relative atomic mass 209.9871479(83), isotopic composition blank; At-211 relative atomic mass 210.9874966(30), isotopic composition blank. A relative atomic mass is scaled to carbon-12. An isotopic composition, when the field is not blank, is a representative mole fraction, not a new assay made for this card. The symbols for an interval, a parenthesis, a bracket, and a # mark are defined on world.chemistry.nist-atomic-weight-notation. This standard atomic weight is not the Chemistry WebBook molecular-weight field, which is a different catalog entry when one exists.
